newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Richter says new plant to comply with FDA rules.
newsitem.headline: Richter says new plant to comply with FDA rules.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals firm Richter Gedeon Rt's planned 100 million German mark plant will comply with U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) rules, thus enabling Richter to export anywhere in the world, the company said on Wdnesday.
"The company's long-term strategy calls for increasing exports of ready products to American and west European markets," Richter said in a statement.
German engineering group Linde AG said earlier that it had won a contract to build a new 100 million mark pharmaceutical plant for Richter, which expects it to be completed by 2000.
The contract covers the full reconstruction of Richter's hormone product maker complex and the modernisation of certain Richter Budapest-based manufacturing units, the statement said.
Richter said Linde will complete these works as a main contractor, using Hungarian sub-contractors.
"This is the biggest individual order to date Linde has won alone in eastern Europe," the statement said, adding that Linde won over U.S. and British rivals.
